We introduce Articulated Neural Rendering (ANR), a new framework for rendering photorealistic images of human figures in arbitrary poses using sparse inputs. Our approach utilizes an image-based neural field that incorporates a skeletal structure to efficiently model articulated bodies. By utilizing skeletal constraints, ANR separates the learning of appearance from pose variations, enabling the synthesis of realistic renders from just a few reference images. Unlike traditional geometry-based modeling, our method uses neural fields to capture high-fidelity surface details such as clothing folds and hair strands. The system is trained in an unstructured manner and supports real-time rendering on a single GPU. We validate our approach on two datasets featuring real photography of clothed individuals, demonstrating superior performance over prior methods. Additionally, we release our rendering pipeline under an open-source license.

The proliferation of image enhancement tools, capable of rendering ordinary photographs extraordinary, has drastically altered the content people view. Yet, little is known regarding how such manipulations affect visual analysis. This study investigates the discrepancies between human and machine sensitivity to changes resulting from various image alterations. Participants and algorithm models were tasked with identifying specific modifications in a subset of images that had been altered in three distinct ways. Results indicate that humans struggle to detect certain changes that machines readily perceive, whereas machines fail to detect changes that humans easily identify. Furthermore, the research examines the machine learning models' ability to anticipate human responses to image alterations. While trained models performed better than humans in specific contexts, they generalized poorly in others compared to human accuracy. Ultimately, these findings suggest that as artificial intelligence increasingly integrates into society, it is imperative to design systems that align with human expectations rather than those that diverge from human nature.

This paper explores how to construct a comprehensive set of symbols for all classical and quantum links using Chern-Simons theory. We demonstrate that the $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ quantum link category serves as the appropriate replacement for the classical case, where the parameter $q$ is set to $1$. We also investigate the connection between the universal central element of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ and the Casimir operator within the Chern-Simons context. We examine the ground state properties of a 2D trimer antiferromagnet featuring weak inter-trimer couplings using spin cluster quantum Monte Carlo (SQMC) and density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) methods. Our findings indicate that the two methods yield consistent results for the low-energy physics of this system. We identify a phase characterized by 1/3 magnetization plateaus alongside specific spin excitations. Additionally, we analyze the susceptibility and specific heat phase diagrams, determining the ratios of inter- and intra-trimer coupling constants required to enter the plateau phase. We further discuss the potential for observing this phase in a quantum simulator based on cold atoms.

Despite the remarkable zero-shot performance of language models, they still require specific adjustments to reach this level. This paper introduces a method that fine-tunes pre-trained models using a curated collection of datasets and classification cues (triggers). By employing the Dataset and Cue Collection (CoCo) framework, we tune an English model on 1,022 datasets containing over 120 million labeled examples across 1,022 distinct classes. These triggers are then used to adapt the model for noun phrase classification. Our findings indicate that such tuning is essential for achieving high-quality zero-shot results. Furthermore, we present a novel training approach that allows a single model to handle both the dataset-specific tasks and the newly introduced zero-shot cue-based tasks.

The two Higgs boson masses detected by the LHC are accurately predicted by a $Z_3$-symmetric Next-to-Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (nNMSM) scenario, which also features a distinct electroweak phase shift (eWPS). In this model, the dark matter candidate is the lightest singlet Higgs boson, and the scenario is consistent with the absence of gravitational wave (GW) signals observed so far. We examine how upcoming GW detection efforts could test this specific nNMSM configuration.

Precise geocoding of astronomical sources is essential for accurately determining their redshifts. We introduce an automated, sub-milliparsec-precision tool for generating and analyzing geographic coordinates and (red)z-geocoding simulations for cosmological parameter estimation. Our work demonstrates that high-fidelity sub-mm geocoding is critical for obtaining unbiased results, particularly in the context of the H$_0$1083 tension. Using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), we conducted a $z$-geocoding simulation for the galaxy NGC 4649, employing both standard and high-precision techniques. We investigate the low-energy dynamical properties of the Heisenberg antiferromagnet on a triangular lattice through large-scale quantum Monte Carlo simulations of the spin-structure factor $S(\mathbf{q},\tau)$ across varying temperatures and imaginary times. By employing maximum-entropy techniques to extract the frequency-dependent spin structure factor $S(\mathbf{q},\omega)$, we identify distinct dynamical regimes corresponding to long-range ordered, disordered, and symmetry-rupted phases. Specifically, we observe a non-analytic transition in the low-frequency limit as the system moves from an ordered state to a symmetry-rupted phase. Furthermore, our results indicate that a quantum-disordered (liquid) phase emerges at lower pressures compared to what conventional static methods predict.

The magnetic ordering in the hexagonal antiferromagnet Cr$_2$Al is investigated through a combination of first-principles calculations, neutron diffraction, and muon spin rotation techniques. Results indicate an in-plane ferromagnetic alignment with an out-of-plane antiferromagnetic arrangement. Analysis of the exchange interactions reveals that the $J_1$ coupling between Cr atoms along the $a$-axis is the most significant, while the $J_2$ interaction between neighboring layers is relatively weak. Furthermore, the muon stopping sites were determined to be $\frac{1}{2}(0,0,z_\mu)$ and $\frac{1}{2}(\bar{1},\bar{1},z_\mu)$, respectively.

This study introduces a new kinetic kinetic model featuring a constant relaxation time that varies with molecular speed, designed to reflect intermolecular potential influences in rarefied gas flows. The model's accuracy is evaluated against direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) data across several benchmark scenarios, including the Couette flow, Poiseuille flow, and the channel flow cases. Results demonstrate that the proposed framework successfully mimics the influence of intermolecular potentials across a broad spectrum of Knudsen numbers.

We introduce a new method for efficiently developing task-specific semantic analyzers. The approach is designed to generate high-quality word-level semantic representations that can subsequently assemble into sentence-level vectors, which serve as robust inputs for downstream applications. The core of this method is a two-stage training process: first, we train representations using a large corpus of unsupervised or unsupervised data; second, we refine these representations to maximize performance on a very small dataset of specific semantic tasks. The approach is grounded in a new training objective that explicitly leverages established principles of compositional semantics. We demonstrate that this method yields significantly better results than current state-of-the-art techniques, particularly when the final training dataset contains only a few hundred examples.

The future Electron-Iron Collider (EIC) is designed to probe the 3D subnuclear architecture of the proton and light ions, advancing our comprehension of the strong force and heavy-quark dynamics. To achieve these objectives, the collider will employ advanced pixel silicon trackers to isolate and precisely measure the trajectories of charged particles. This review examines the cutting-edge silicon sensor technologies currently under investigation for EIC applications.

The variability observed in the continuum emissions of low-mass active galactic nuclei (AGN) has not been adequately studied. We analyze the optical continuum fluctuations of the low-mass AGN, NGC 4395, using 12 years of photometric data from the ZTF survey. Our results indicate that the object exhibits both stochastic and quasi-periodic (QP) variations. While the QP signal is detected in the optical range, it is not the dominant feature; instead, the optical light curve is primarily shaped by occasional outbursts. These outbursts are characterized by a QP component with a period of approximately 1.1 days, which is most pronounced during the object's maximum brightness. We propose that these outbursts are triggered by non-stationary accretion events, such as the clumpy nature of the inner disk or global disk oscillations.

We present a bosonic representation for the one-dimensional Gosinski (Dunkl) operator, derived from the representation $\sigma$ of the Bose algebra generated by a single bosonic algebra. The representation of Dunkl's first intertwining link is denoted by $\tau$, acting between the polynomial ring $\mathbb{C}[x]$ and the symmetric Fock space $\Gamma_h (L^2(\mathbb{C}))$, where $h$ is the parameter. The study examines the decomposition of $\tau$ into irreducible components. The decomposition is linked to the classical Hermite polynomials, the deformed Hermite polynomials introduced by Szegő, and the polynomials defined by Shohat within the context of the symmetric subspaces of $\Gamma_h (L^2(\mathbb{C}))$. The analysis establishes the orthogonality of the deformed Hermite poloids and derives an explicit formula for their generating series. Furthermore, the study investigates the asymptotic behavior of the polynomials of order $n$ as $n$ tends to infinity.

We present ALMA observations of the H30$\alpha$ line within NGC 5253, a galaxy characterized by low metallicity, to investigate its star formation activity. The data reveal a compact H30$\alpha$ core situated in the northern region of NGC 5253, which exhibits a flux of 0.000030 Jy km s$^{-1}$. This core is spatially correlated with a CO(2-1) component displaying a flux of 0.030 Jy km s$^{-1}$. By analyzing the H30$\alpha$ and CO(2-1) fluxes, we derive a correction factor of 0.030 for the line ratio R(H30$\alpha$/CO(2-1)). This ratio indicates that the core's metallicity is approximately 0.030 times that of the Sun. Additionally, we estimate the H2 molecular mass in the CO(2-1) component to be approximately 0.030 solar masses, yielding an SFR/MH2 ratio of approximately 0.030 s$^{-1}$. These findings suggest that the core's metallicity and star formation rate are approximately 0.030 times and solar values, respectively.

This paper examines the asymptotic properties of Nadaraya-Watson estimators, which serve as popular nonparametric methods for estimating conditional expectation functions. The analysis covers univariate and multivariate scenarios, utilizing various smoothing techniques such as kernels, regression splines, and splines. Additionally, we evaluate the theoretical behavior of Nadaraya-Watson estimators in scenarios where the conditional expectation function exhibits a finite degree of smoothness and the kernel functions are characterized by finite moments and satisfy specific boundary conditions. The results indicate that the estimators possess a consistent property and that their asymptotic distribution converges to a normal distribution. The convergence rate depends on the degree of smoothness of the underlying function and the order of the kernel function used. The theoretical results are illustrated using numerical examples and compared with other nonparametric methods for estimating conditional expectation functions.

A novel framework is introduced to observe and track the progression of epidemics. This approach relies on a nonlinear dynamic model that captures the interplay between population dynamics and environmental factors to define the observer structure. A defining feature of this framework is its ability to adapt dynamically to specific epidemic characteristics by modifying model parameters and selecting appropriate observer designs. This flexibility allows for the precise estimation of critical epidemiological metrics, such as the basic reproduction number ($R_0$) and the disease elimination threshold, while simultaneously identifying the optimal timing for implementing control measures.

Predicting the future evolution of Knowledge Graphs (KGs) is a critical challenge in the realm of Knowledge Graph Completion. While numerous existing studies address this by leveraging temporal modeling frameworks to predict future entity relationships, the current work explores the effectiveness of static modeling structures for the same goal. Our approach involves training a static model on a KG snapshot and evaluating its performance on subsequent, later-time graph instances. To evaluate this, we conducted extensive experiments across multiple standard static models and assessed them on three well-established datasets. Our findings indicate that static frameworks can achieve performance comparable to, or even superior to, dynamic temporal models under certain circumstances.

Ultrashort pulse lasers, known for their high peak power, have become essential tools across numerous scientific and industrial disciplines. Kerr-lens mode-locking (KLMM) stands out as the most effective technique for generating these pulses within oscillators. This study presents a rigorous geometric examination of KLMM aimed at maximizing the cavity's Kerr-lensing aperture. The analysis indicates that for pulses with a duration of 100 fs, the aperture is maximized when the lens is placed at the waist of the fundamental cavity mode, which occurs at approximately 13.5 cm from the amplifier mirror. Furthermore, the research shows that KLMM can be sustained with a gain medium aperture of up to 100 µm, provided the laser crystal is positioned at the waist of the fundamental cavity mode.

This work addresses the nonlinear regression challenge of harnessing data from an asynchronous, resource-limited network of edge devices. We introduce a new asynchronous online federated learning algorithm, which allows devices to contribute individually to model updates without requiring the global model to be stopped or slowed. We establish convergence guarantees for this method, demonstrating that the proposed approach achieves a risk error of $O(\frac{\log(T)}{T})$ as $T$ approaches infinity, where $T$ denotes the total count of samples processed. We validate the method through extensive simulations using an asynchronous federated learning architecture, employing the $k$-nearest neighbors algorithm for nonlinear regression tasks. These simulations demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the k-nearest neighbors approach by a factor of 2.5 in risk error and surpasses the Online Federated Linear method by a factor of 3.5 in the same metric.

We introduce a new family of high-dimensional expander graph constructs derived from the geometry of Riemannian manifoms and finite group actions, utilizing the Cayley Cayley-Ritz matrices associated with these phenomena. Our approach involves two distinct methods: the first involves defining graphs based on the unit tangent bundle's vertex set and the action of the high-dimensional expander, while the second relies on the use of specific finite subgroups within the unit tangent space as nodes for graph construction. We demonstrate that these graphs possess the properties of high-dimensional expanders, which has numerous applications in high-dimensional analysis and theoretical computer science.

This study investigates the magnetic properties of GdInO$_3$ through DC and AC susceptibility as well as magnetization measurements across various field orientations. Data from DC susceptibility and magnetization experiments indicate a Néel temperature of approximately 10 K, with a broad temperature range between 10 K and 100 K displaying field-cooled and zero-field-cooled susceptibility splitting. The magnetization vs. field data, analyzed using models for both collinear and non-collinear antiferromagnetic (AFM) structures, are best explained by a hexagonal-type AFM arrangement. Furthermore, the application of a magnetic field perpendicular to the crystallographic c-axis induces a metamagnetic transition at low fields, whereas parallel field orientations show this transition only at significantly higher field strengths. These findings, combined with susceptibility data, support a magnetic structure where Gd ions are arranged in alternating up-down-up-down fashion within the honeycomb layers, with the magnetic moments oriented perpendicular to the ab-plane. Additionally, AC susceptibility measurements reveal a phase shift in the imaginary component that grows with decreasing frequency and exhibits a peak at 100 K, which is attributed to the dynamics of glassy spins trapped in a complex energy landscape.

Link prediction is a critical capability for network analysis, particularly in NLP contexts where entities are mapped to networks and interactions are modeled as edges. While Subspace Skip-Gram (SG) serves as a standard approach for network embedding, it is ill-suited for Link Prediction in sparse networks because it relies on computing global word (or edge) co-occurrence statistics. To address this, we introduce Sparse Subspace Network Embedding (SSNE), an efficient method that derives local node representations without requiring full co-occurrence matrices. By focusing on sparse neighborhoods, SSNE enhances the accuracy of Link Prediction in sparse environments. Furthermore, we develop a rapid prediction strategy that accelerates inference, and our experiments demonstrate that SSNE outperforms current state-of-the-art methods, especially in terms of precision for sparse network applications.

We present the fabrication and testing of silicon atomic vapor chambers featuring a depth of 300 micrometers and dimensions of 2 cm by 2 cm, achieved through the use of deep silicon anisotropic etching. These chambers are micro-fabricated to include integrated optical windows, electrical feedthroughs, and a window frame. The devices are evaluated using Raman spectroscopy to assess the quality of the window frame and by trapping rubidium atoms to evaluate the window transmission. Additionally, the chambers are examined using a Zeeman slow beam to determine light capture efficiency. This study demonstrates that the etching process successfully produces chambers with high-quality optical interfaces suitable for advanced atomic research applications.

In contemporary optical communication, four-dimensional (4D) modulation formats utilizing dual-polarization have gained significant traction. This study introduces a novel modeling method for linear and nonlinear interference power across dual-polarization 4D formats. The model incorporates the nonlinear Schrodinger equation, the vector sum approximation, and the Gaussian noise approximation. Crucially, it accounts for the mutual influence of nonlinear disturbances between channels in all three spatial dimensions. Validation against the vector sum of the nonlinear Schrodinger equations confirms the accuracy of this approach.

Recent advancements in deep learning have facilitated the development of numerous image fusion methodologies. Among these, deep learning-based approaches have garnered significant attention due to their exceptional performance. This study introduces FIRe-GAN, a novel deep learning-driven fusion framework designed to merge visible and infrared imagery specifically for wildfire detection. FIRe-GAN leverages a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) architecture equipped with a generator and a discriminator. The generator employs two key components: a spatial feature extraction module and a spectral feature extraction module. These components process spectral data from input images to generate GAN-compatible features, which are then utilized to reconstruct the final fused result. The discriminator assesses the realism of the generator's output and the GAN compatibility of the intermediate features. FIRe-GAN was evaluated against three existing fusion methods using a benchmark dataset of wildfire visible-infrared pairs. The results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms current techniques in both quantitative metrics and qualitative visual inspection.

Social media platforms are increasingly utilized for gathering information regarding users' physical and mental health. This study presents a novel method for identifying indicators of depression within social media content, grounded in the semantic association between positive and negative emotions reflected in postings. The proposed approach involves processing text through Natural Language Processing (NLP) to derive features, which are then analyzed using Support Vector Regression (SVR) to quantify emotional positivity/negativity. These results are subsequently evaluated against established metrics to determine the presence of depressive signs. The work also details the construction of a new depression detection dataset, which consists of Twitter profiles tagged by the National Institute of Mental Health as experiencing severe depression. The SVR model was trained and tested on this dataset, yielding an Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (ROC) of 0.72 and an Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve of 0.62.

This study utilizes a stochastic compartmental framework to model the rapid expansion of COVID-19 cases. The research model is constructed by integrating a random process into a deterministic compartmental system, specifically representing the daily new infections as independent and identically distributed random variables. Key characteristics of this model include its ability to compute fundamental quantities such as the expected number of daily new cases, mean value for the basic reproductive number ($\mathcal{R}_0$), mean value of the infectious period, and the expected total disease prevalence. Additionally, the model's application to COVID-19 data from the United Kingdom demonstrates that the reproductive number declines as the infection spreads, while the average duration individuals remain infectious is approximately 16 days.

The isoscalar giant monopole resonance in the nuclei $^{24}$Mg and $^{28}$Si was investigated using inelastic scattering of 238 MeV/nucleon $\alpha$-particles, with data compared against a theoretical analysis utilizing a relativistic random phase approximation (RRPM) model. This theoretical framework accounts for the coupling between monopole and quadrupole excitations, with coupling strengths derived from the experimental isoscalar quadrupole resonance (ISQR) data. The ISQR energy and width for the low-lying $2^+$ state in $^{28}$Si were extracted from the $^{24}$Mg reaction, yielding an energy of $2.39 \pm 0.03$ MeV and a width of $0.03 \pm 0.01$ MeV. These measurements indicate that the ISQR in $^{28}$Si is notably narrower than the typical values observed in other nuclei. Furthermore, the study reveals a strong correlation between the ISQR width and the intensity of the high-energy $2^+$ resonance in $^{24}$Mg, which influences the magnitude of the coupling between monopole and quadrupole components. Consequently, this coupling significantly affects the resonance's observed energy and width.

This study examines the convergence behavior of feedback-regulated systems modeled by a second-order nonlinear ordinary differential equation that incorporates both Coulomb friction and Coulomb nonlinearities in the restoring force. We establish sufficient criteria to guarantee that the closed-loop system exhibits either convergent or oscillatory stick-slip motion. These findings are validated through a representative example demonstrating sustained oscillations, alongside the identification of specific convergence conditions for two classes of two-stick sliding friction models.

Agent-based systems are increasingly common in critical sectors like finance and medicine, where agents must make decisions under uncertainty with the potential to impact human safety. Ensuring these agents adhere to rigorous safety standards is therefore essential. This work introduces a new safety mechanism termed Bellman Hedging, which is a no-regret algorithm tailored for multi-armed bandit scenarios. The strategy functions by weighting future expected rewards based on their associated risks, resulting in a conservative policy that remains safe even in worst-case situations. Theoretically, the algorithm achieves a regret bound of $O(\sqrt{T\log K})$ within a finite time horizon $T$, involving $K$ multi-armed options. This theoretical guarantee holds regardless of whether outcomes are stochastic, adversarial, or a mixture of both. Empirical results demonstrate that Bellman Hedging outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods in worst-case regret by a factor of up to 10. Additionally, the approach is easily adaptable to complex settings involving partial observability and continuous action spaces.

Although sequential recommenders are effective, they often fail to uncover the specific reasons driving user behavior. To address this gap, we introduce a neural network-based model designed to explicitly model latent motivations behind user actions. This model utilizes a dual-encoder architecture: a user encoder captures the sequential actions of the individual, while a motivation encoder extracts the corresponding underlying drives. These encoders interact through an attention mechanism to mutually refine their representations, thereby enhancing the overall precision of the recommendations. Evaluations on three datasets confirm that our method significantly boosts the accuracy of sequential recommendations. Furthermore, it outperforms established state-of-the-art techniques in extracting motivation information, demonstrating superior capability in uncovering hidden user drivers compared to existing methods.

The present work examines the double confluent Heun equation (DCHE) arising from two identical, equidistantly positioned singularities of arbitrary strength within a general symmetric configuration. We demonstrate that this equation governs the evolution of a $1+1$-dimensional wave equation, which is equivalent to a Schrödinger-type framework. This describes wave propagation in the presence of a barrier featuring a double-exponential potential. Notably, this potential, while not admitting analytical transmission and reflection coefficients, supports analytical bound state solutions. Furthermore, Heun's equation undergoes a parametric transformation into the trigonometric Heun equation (TCE). In this specific limit, a single transmission coefficient becomes expressible in closed form as a function of the barrier parameters. Finally, we analyze the inverse problem for the DCHE, detailing how the distribution of eigenvalues within the spectrum maps to characteristics of an underlying square-well-type potential.

This paper introduces essential limits for recovering expressions within a subspace defined by low-rank heterogeneity, where data points exhibit varying but low-rank structures. We focus on the optimal performance attainable using a single estimator for this task. First, we establish a fundamental lower bound that depends on the specific ranks and dimensions of the individual components. Second, we propose an OLS-based estimator capable of achieving optimal convergence rates when the number of components is small. Furthermore, when dealing with a large number of components, we develop a computationally efficient alternative utilizing the groupwise singular value decomposition (SVD) that also achieves optimal rates. Finally, we validate the effectiveness of these methods through simulations and apply them to a real-world dataset.

Tunneling experiments reveal a complete absence of Andreev reflection on graphene nanoribbon (GNR) edges lacking inversion symmetry, an observation that seems to contradict standard theory. We resolve this paradox by demonstrating that the conductance is governed not by edge states, but by the topology of the entire system. The study demonstrates that this behavior stems from a novel class of topological protection rooted in the chiral symmetry inherent to GNRs. The research further shows that the conductance remains robust despite perturbations that disrupt edge-state conformal symmetries, provided they preserve the bulk chiral symmetry. Additionally, the analysis indicates that the conductance scales with the number of graphene atoms, and the characteristic length of the oscillations is determined by the system's size.

Driven by the rapid global spread of the SARS-CoV-2 virus and the consequent challenges to healthcare systems, this study introduces a deep learning framework designed to manage infected patients. Furthermore, we establish that a theory remains self-consistent only when its constituent S-matrix satisfies specific criteria, such as ensuring a determinate system of equations and guaranteeing a non-zero Wronskian.

Utilizing the frequency multiplier method alongside a novel test function approach, we demonstrate that both static (static) and dynamic (dynamic) strategies can achieve uniform stabilization of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations within critical $L^q$-based Sobolev and Besov spaces. Specifically, our findings confirm that open-closed-loop systems stabilize the incompressible fluid flow in a significantly faster timeframe than open-closed-loop (static) systems. These results extend previous work by the authors [20, 21], which addressed similar stabilization issues for the incompressible Euler and Burgers equations.

Lexicons are essential resources for enhancing language models, yet constructing a new one demands significant effort and financial investment. To address this, we introduce LitMind, a newly developed online dictionary offering an user-friendly environment for the creation, editing, and collaboration on linguistic resources. Drawing inspiration from successful encyclopedias and leveraging existing linguistic infrastructure, the system is designed to lower the technical barriers for building collaborative lexica. By facilitating the integration of existing data and supporting specialized features like synonymy and synonym links, the tool also boosts the semantic depth of language models.

Recommendation systems increasingly rely on explainability to enhance system performance, foster user trust, and encourage engagement. This study evaluates explanation quality across three critical dimensions: commitment (the extent to which a recommendation remains valid when supported by an explanation), stability (the consistency of explanations given similar data), and stability (the consistency of explanations given identical systems but varying users). We analyze these properties within the LIME-RS framework, a LIME variant designed specifically for recommendation tasks. Our findings indicate that while commitments are generally low, explanations generated by LIME-RS are stable for the same user but lack robustness regarding other tested scenarios. This work offers the initial empirical investigation into the commitment and stability of explanation-based recommendations, shedding light on the intricate relationship between explanatory text and algorithmic suggestions.

This study examines Fermi level pinning in InAs quantum wells on indium antimonide substrates, utilizing both experimental measurements and theoretical modeling. Experimental results indicate that the electron carrier concentration within the quantum wells is highly sensitive to a surface dipole layer, which can be regulated by applying an external electric field. Theoretical analysis attributes this behavior to the formation of a dipole layer at the air/semiconductor interface, arising from the interaction between surface states and bulk charge carriers. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that the energy position of these surface states can be significantly altered by a strategically placed surface charge layer. These findings underscore the critical importance of near-surface regions in semiconductor heterostructures and illustrate their potential for active electronic manipulation.

Recent research has demonstrated that Resilient Learning (RL) can effectively train deep neural networks (DNNs) against a broad spectrum of adversarial threats. However, RL is not a universal solution; its efficacy hinges on the specific task and the nature of the attacks employed. This study investigates the attributes of a task and the query regions utilized in RL that facilitate efficacy. We demonstrate that a task is amenable to Resilious Learning when Regional Queries are beneficial, and conversely, RL is most advantageous when such queries aid convergence. We further provide a theoretical justification for why Regional Queries are helpful in specific contexts and demonstrate that their utility extends to a variety of both classification and regression problems. Additionally, we find that Reginald Queries can assist RL in navigating challenging convergence scenarios, and our experiments reveal that both the choice of attack and the region shape significantly impact task success.

In recent years, the Sinkhorn algorithm has become a popular choice for solving large-scale optimal transport problems. However, its standard implementation relies on a doubly stochastic matrix iteration, which is inherently slow. This paper introduces Quick Sinkhorn II (QS2), a new algorithm that breaks down the original problem into a sequence of smaller subproblems. Each subproblem is solved using a closed-form formula, allowing QS2 to be significantly more efficient than the original Sinkhorn method. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that QS2 is a direct extension of the original Sinkhorn algorithm, and numerical experiments confirm that QS2 achieves a speedup of up to 100x compared to the original Sinkhorn algorithm.

This study presents the most comprehensive analysis of FUV variability in AU Mic to date, utilizing 12 years of HST G140L observations. We detect a significant increase in G140L flux during flares, indicating that these events are driven by hot magnetosphere emission rather than just enhanced chromospheric activity. Specifically, flares boost flux by a factor of 2.5 in the HST G140L filter and by 3.5 when normalized to the rest of the instrument's response. We identify three distinct quiescent states for the star: G140L fluxes of 0.0001, 0.0002, and 0.0004 erg cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$, which correspond to rotational phase angles of 0.7, 0.7, 0.7, 0.7, 0.7, 0.7, 0.7, 0.7, 0.7, 0.7, 0.7, 0.7, 0.7, 0.7, 0.7, 0.7, 0.7, 0.7, 0.7, 0.7, 0.7, 0.7, 0.7, 0.7, 0.7, 0.

We analyze the dynamics of a heavy particle traversing an ionic fluid modeled as a resistive continuum, where particle motion generates an electromagnetic field that performs back-reaction work on the system. The analysis incorporates both stochastic electromagnetic fluctuations and the medium's equilibrium electron distribution, with the latter treated in a classical framework. Classical resistance effects are integrated into an extended Langevin equation that explicitly accounts for the radiation force. The study derives frequency-dependent resistivity and susceptibility measures for this novel system, with the response mechanisms modulated by the heavy particle's mass.

In this study, we tackle the challenge of classifying new observations within imbalanced datasets. Traditional Closest Neighbor (CNN) classification often fails in such scenarios because it treats all samples as equally significant, which can lead to biased predictions. To address this limitation, we introduce a statistical approach that assigns appropriate weights to CNN predictions. The method calculates these weights to account for the imbalances, and its effectiveness is validated through experiments on four real-world imbalanced datasets.

We introduce an updated catalog of 1,000 bright (r < 17.5) quasars at high redshift (3 < z < 6.5) derived from SkyMapper observations, designed to facilitate investigations into the co-evolution of supermassive black holes and their host galaxies. This compilation merges data from three prior publications with a newly identified set of 250 quasars, including 100 from the r < 17.5 sample and 150 from the r < 19 sample. The catalog is complete to r < 17.5 for z > 3.5 and r > 17.5 for z > 3.5. We detail the catalog's characteristics, such as source positions, magnitudes, and redshifts, and provide comprehensive data on variability, host galaxy properties, and nuclear characteristics. Additionally, we present updated quasar luminosity functions (QLFs) for the r < 17.5 magnitude cut, which exhibit a "luminous end" characterized by a slope of d log $\lambda$ Q/d log $\lambda$ L = 1.45 $\pm$ 0.05 at z = 3.5, a steeper gradient than previously reported. This steepening is attributed to the inclusion of newly discovered ultra-luminous quasars in our extended catalog.

This study investigates the tunneling dynamics between a quantum dot and a superconducting lead using gate sensing techniques. We demonstrate that gate sensing can detect the average charge within the quantum dot even when tunneling occurs via multiple pathways involving Cooper pairs from the superconducting lead. Furthermore, we establish that superconductivity within the lead can be utilized to enhance gate sensing sensitivity. These findings offer a pathway to achieve precise measurements of charge states in quantum dots coupled to superconducting reservoirs, a capability essential for the development of superconducting spin qubits and devices based on these systems.

Conservative solutions to systems of conservation laws are often understood as fixed points of specific operator contractions. This study establishes necessary conditions for these entropic contrainers to be unique within appropriate function spaces $L^{\infty}$. Such $L^{\infty}$-contractions correspond to time-dependent functions of an $L^{\infty}$-traveling profile. By formulating these results in the context of $L^{\infty}$-semigroups, we demonstrate that a traveling wave $u_{\rm tw}$ is the sole $\mathcal C^0$-semigroup fixed point, a condition equivalent to $\mathcal C^0$-semigroups being non-periodic. This latter property represents a necessary and sufficient criterion for $\mathcal C^0$-semigroups to lack periodicity, thereby confirming that $u_{\rm tw}$ is a $L^{\infty}$-semigroup non-periodicity. This finding highlights a specific subclass of $L^{\infty}$-semigroups which exhibit periodicity in their associated $L^{\infty}$-semigroups. This paper introduces **DiffDreamer**, an innovative conditional diffusion architecture designed for high-fidelity, consistent free-viewport generation from a single static image. Unlike many existing approaches that depend on pre-trained large-scale 3D priors or require auxiliary data like multi-view images or textual metadata, DiffDreamer leverages a text-to-image diffusion model as its foundational prior. By employing a geometrically grounded prompt expansion strategy, it effectively bridges the capability gap between diffusion systems and typical 3D representations. Furthermore, it implements a dual-stage training framework: an initial pre-training phase establishes foundational 3D priors, followed by fine-tuning to acquire specific object attributes. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate that DiffDreamer surpasses current state-of-the-art methods in terms of both visual fidelity and geometric accuracy.

This work presents a novel framework designed to forecast, augment, and manage networked phenomena, grounded in the principle that a system's dynamics are captured by the temporal evolution of its order parameter, which links microscopic details to macroscopic behavior. We introduce a straightforward data-driven method to derive this order parameter, utilizing the principal direction of fluctuations from a reference state. This approach facilitates the prediction, upscaling, and control of various processes, especially those where a phase transition occurs. Validating the framework's utility, we apply it to the SIS epidemic model, demonstrating that it successfully anticipates first-order phase transitions in phase space, optimally controls the prevalence of infection, and explains the phenomenon of optimal enhancement through a first-principles perspective.

This study examines the instability driving drop formation on solid cylindrical fibers coated with a thin liquid film, a process known as the Rayleigh-Plateau instability. It was discovered that surface slip significantly accelerates drop nucleation, a finding attributed to slip-induced draining that thins the liquid film more effectively than standard viscous dissipation alone. Furthermore, an analytical model incorporating this slip effect reveals that, unlike scenarios with no slip, drop formation can occur on horizontal fibers, a consequence of a fundamental shift in the instability's character.

This study establishes lipchitz stability for the formal in verse formula known as the Hunter-Saxton formula, which connects solutions of the classical H-S equation to modified equations involving delays and derivatives. We demonstrate that when the initial data changes within the space of $k$-times continuously differentiable functions, the corresponding solutions change in a $C^k$-smooth and lipchitz manner with respect to time.

Robotic ultrasound is a promising new approach for scoliosis assessment, yet its consistency and accuracy relative to expert manual imaging remain uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate reliability by comparing robotic ultrasound measurements against those taken manually by experts. The research involved 30 scoliosis patients scanned with both methods at the apex and topmost curves, with a 2-week interval between scans. A radiologist performed manual scans and analyzed them offline, while the same radiologist repeated the analysis of robotic scans after the delay. Scoliosis was quantified using both Cobb angle (C.A.) and dynamic angle measurements (D.A.M.). The manual and robotic results were compared using Bland-Altman plots, while repeatability was assessed via intra-class correlation coefficients (I.C.C.). The data showed that both techniques yielded comparable precision and accuracy. Furthermore, both methods demonstrated high repeatability, with I.C.C. values exceeding 0.80 for all measurements. These findings suggest that robotic ultrasound offers a reliable, consistent, and accurate alternative to traditional manual scoliosis imaging.

Although text-to-speech (TSP) synthesis has advanced significantly, it remains predominantly utilized for generating audio from short phrases rather than full conversational content. This limitation arises from the fact that synthetic audio is typically modeled using parametric or neural coding schemes, which rely on statistical techniques to synthesize speech based on acoustic models. However, statistical modeling proves inadequate for long-form text due to the immense volume of required acoustic data. This paper introduces a non-statistical approach to determine the appropriate duration of synthetic speech for given textual inputs. By employing a median calculation, the proposed method effectively addresses the statistical challenges associated with long-form synthesis, thereby enhancing the accuracy of speech time estimation for extended texts.

This study introduces a new approach to detecting hate speech, which is increasingly challenging due to evolving linguistic patterns and content types. The paper outlines the proposed system, which centers on modeling the interactions between content and text through a new method for handling different data modalities. By integrating these heterogeneous signals, the approach enhances the robustness of the resulting feature representations. Experimental results demonstrate that this model achieves superior performance compared to existing methods on the highly challenging multi-lingual HASOC 2019 benchmark.

This study introduces a multi-input multi-output (MIMO) framework designed to concurrently address multiple classification categories. While the architecture features two distinct feature extractors, they are not fully independent; instead, they engage in selective feature sharing. Specifically, the architecture allows the second feature extractor to utilize outputs from the first, yet prevents reverse sharing. This asymmetric interaction is managed through a dynamic gate mechanism that determines how much of its own features the second extracts can access from the first. The primary objective is to enhance the model's efficiency by facilitating feature reuse. Experimental results indicate that this approach yields performance equivalent to a stack of two separate feature extractors, confirming that effective feature sharing is achievable even when the second extractor depends on the first.

This paper provides a comprehensive review of datasets for historical image collections, covering the scope, composition, and technical specifications of each. It further examines the primary applications for these data resources, such as optical character recognition, image restoration, and other related tasks. Finally, the work outlines the current limitations and future directions for scholarly research in this domain.

This work presents the development of a control framework designed to enhance trajectory tracking accuracy and reduce jerk in industrial robots, which typically suffer from limited encoder precision. The proposed approach employs auxiliary encoders alongside standard position sensors to substantially boost position tracking performance. Furthermore, it implements specific jerk-limiting control mechanisms to ensure smoother robot joint movements. The integrated system combines these strategies to boost overall robot operational efficiency. Experimental results validate the system's efficacy, demonstrating marked improvements in trajectory accuracy, jerk reduction, and movement smoothness.

This study examines whether the multiple state examination method—which accounts for the interdependence of recurrent, mutually exclusive health states—can enhance the identification of distinct myocardial infarction (MI) trajectories. Utilizing data from the National Long-Term Care Survey, we constructed a binary time-to-occurrence model for MI and a proportional hazards analysis for post-MI nursing home admission. Our findings indicate that while MI trajectory risk is significantly elevated among those with a family history of the disease, a low education level, and a diagnosis prior to age 70, incorporating post-ADMISSION nursing home admission into the analysis reveals additional insights. Specifically, patients with a family history of MI exhibit significantly higher risks of entering nursing care following an MI event. Furthermore, including the post-incident trajectory uncovers distinct MI paths that the initial models alone fail to detect.

Molecular dynamics simulations frequently rely on the NVT ensemble, which necessitates a coupling between the system and a heat bath. In this study, we propose a quadrature method designed to integrate such continuous environments into the molecular equations of motion. Specifically, the method models the heat bath's influence as both dissipative forces and an stochastic NVT thermostatting potential. The resulting equations of motion constitute a deterministic-quasistochastic hybrid system addressed via a quadrature scheme that employs multiple-site principles alongside a velocity Verlet discretization. The approach was validated through simulations of a harmonic oscillator and a benzene molecule, demonstrating the ability to regulate both the average temperature and statistical distribution.

The metric dimension of a graph $G$ refers to the smallest cardinality of a vertex subset $S$ where any two distinct vertices differ by having different distances to at least one member within $S$. This parameter is $k$-fixed in a graph class $\mathcal{G}$ if every graph in that class has metric dimension no exceeding $k$. This work establishes that the parameter of being less than or equal to $k$ is both $k$-fixed and $k$-large, where a class $\mathcal{G}$ is $k$-large when the removal of any vertex eliminates at least $k$ edges. Leveraging this insight, we demonstrate that both metric dimension and the vertex metric dimension are $k$-fixed and $k$-large for structural factors such as feedback vertex groups, segment size in vertex segments, and those in full graph segment decompositions. These findings are significant because they yield the inaugural polynomial-time fixed-parameter tractable (FPT) algorithms capable of computing these specific structural parameters.

Directed hom-type theory, which studies the homotopy theory of directed spaces, utilizes specific tools such as direction functions to determine when a directed space permits directed homotopy equivalence. This work introduces authority functions, a broader category of tools that are at least as effective as direction functions for this purpose. We establish several fundamental properties of authority functions and demonstrate their application through two distinct types: global authority functions and local authority functions. Global authority functions are defined by using directed colimits to construct functors on a directed category, whereas local authority functions are defined by using directed limits to construct functors on a directed category.

The Earth's cryosphere is anticipated to warm considerably over the coming centuries, which could result in dramatic shifts in the global hydrological cycle. However, precise forecasts regarding future precipitation and runoff remain elusive. Consequently, we utilize a high-resolution Earth System Model (CESM2) to explore the evolution of the hydrological cycle under greenhouse gas forcing scenarios, specifically targeting climates warmer than current Earth standards. Our analysis indicates that, relative to present-day conditions, simulated climates warmer than 2°C exhibit more pronounced episodic flooding events. These frequent inundations are driven by an enhanced atmospheric moisture capacity and a reduced likelihood of precipitation reaching the land surface.

In generalized self-dual Yang-Mills theory, where the gauge group is replaced by a principal bundle over a variety $X$ with the group being higher than $GL(n,\mathbb{C})$, the theory retains only its holomorphic self-dual component of the curvature. This paper demonstrates that within such a broader self-dual Yang-Mills framework, physical states can be constructed using standard twistor methods. These constructions yield an affine symmetry, specifically the group $GL(X)$, acting on the bundle. By employing this $GL(X)$ symmetry, a consistent generalization of the Yang-Mills equations to arbitrary higher groups is achieved. Furthermore, the text establishes that while the $GL(X)$ invariance persists, the resulting gauge-invariant observables are strictly local, relying exclusively on curvature data at a specific point on $X$. Finally, the analysis extends the holomorphic self-dual Yang-Mills theory to include anti-locality, yielding a further generalized set of equations whose solutions are shown to correspond to the second-order partial differential equations defined on the manifold $X$.

In the realm of medical image analysis, the quality of data annotation is paramount to model performance. Despite this necessity, human experts frequently introduce errors during the labeling process, leading to significant model performance degradation. This study introduces a novel Bayesian-driven mechanism for renovating label renovations to address labeling discrepancies specifically within the category classification of medical images. By integrating this mechanism with an efficient convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture, the work demonstrates substantial improvements in accuracy for diagnostic image classification.

This study establishes a refined upper bound for the norm of an interpolation operator defined on the interval $I=[-1,1]$ within the space $C(I)$ for any arbitrary node configuration $\{x_j\}_{j=0}^n \subset I$. Consequently, it demonstrates that for the barycentric interpolation operator specified by distinct points $\{x_j\}_{j=0}^n \subset I$, the associated norm remains bounded by an absolute constant independent of $n$.

We investigate a class of polynomials defined over non-negative real numbers that take values between 0 and 1 and constitute a subset of monic transition probability matrices for specific random walks. Within this category, there exists a unique subclass where the sum of the first and second-degree polynomial coefficients equals exactly 1. The polynomials and the corresponding random walks are intrinsically linked through the graph's structure, with both sharing the same degree. The paper addresses the characterization and classification of these polynomials and their associated random walks, with a particular emphasis on graphs containing exactly five vertices. Additionally, we present and demonstrate a method for constructing a polynomial with a prescribed set of roots.

We introduce a timable definition framework within HOL, applicable to all functions exhibiting timability. This capability allows HOL to automatically generate timing annotations for such functions during the development process. Furthermore, this framework supports the definition of relations and equations. Definitions can also be overridden to adjust timing annotations without altering the function's behavior, and we provide formal proofs that the resulting timed definitions preserve both equivalence with the original definition and timability.

This study introduces a data-informed methodology designed to refine modeling approaches for predicting instantaneous turbulent flows. The approach utilizes machine learning techniques to map discrepancies between model outputs and high-fidelity data, with the primary objective of enhancing a wall-bounded turbulence model. Specifically, an improved version of the coherent structure-based (CSB) model is developed by integrating predicted modeling errors. The enhanced strategy is evaluated across two distinct configurations: one utilizing Reynolds shear stress errors and another incorporating predictions of the difference between total and mean kinetic energy. Results indicate that incorporating these estimated errors significantly enhances prediction accuracy. Furthermore, an energy spectrum analysis reveals that the model utilizing kinetic energy differences more accurately reflects the characteristics of canonical wall turbulence, particularly by better capturing the universal energy spectrum range.

This study examines a Born-Infeld infant Skyrme model designed to generate self-dual soliton solutions. The resulting family of these solvations is characterized by a single free parameter, and their specific energy, size, and charge profiles are analyzed. Additionally, the paper investigates the behavior of these solvons under mutual scattering.

The Hofstadter problem describes a square lattice subjected to an incommensurate magnetic flux, yielding a spectrum characterized by fractal complexity. While previous research has explored various limits of this model, a complete phase diagram remains elusive. This work introduces a novel phase: a time-reversal-breaking Weyl semimetal situated within the Hofstadter regime. We demonstrate that the phase diagram undergoes a metal-to-semimetal transition as the magnetic flux approaches commensurability. Furthermore, we examine the properties of the resulting Weyl fermions and propose a viable physical platform for their realization.

To achieve a hybrid nanoantenna combining dielectric and plasmonic characteristics, we utilized finite element method simulations. This hybrid structure features a gold nanoparticle (acting as a scattering element) positioned at the surface of a silicon sphere. Analysis of the optical near-field demonstrated that light is confined to a sub-wavelength scale at both the dielectric and plasmonic interfaces, resulting in significantly enhanced emission from an atom-like dipole emitter. Furthermore, we established that optimizing the position of the gold nanoparticle relative to the sphere allows precise tuning of the scattering cross-section. Ultimately, we showed that a optimized configuration not only boosts the coupling between the sphere and the emitter but also drives efficient, highly directional two-way scattering. This capability effectively separates the emission components of the individual dipole emitter and the sphere, facilitating the creation of efficient, luminous, and highly unidirectional quantum photon sources.

This study introduces an innovative screening mechanism for contact forces in granular materials, which accounts for the spatial separation of tensile and compressive forces. The approach is validated through a finite element method analysis of a two-dimensional shear box, demonstrating strong agreement with experimental data. The optimization process involved tuning a single dimensionless parameter derived from theoretical considerations. The anomalous screening model significantly enhances the performance of the Discrete Element Method (DEM) simulations, resulting in notably improved accuracy.

Using first-principles calculations, we investigate the electronic and magnetic properties of silicon monolayer (Si) decorated on a hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) substrate. We analyze various Mn adsorption configurations, examining how hBN affects the Si layer's electronic structure and exploring the spin-dependent electronic characteristics resulting from Mn decoration. Our findings indicate that while the si monolayer's intrinsic band gap is eliminated upon hBN underlay, the hybridization between Si and hBN states generates a narrow-band gap in the lower spin channel when Mn is adsorbed. Furthermore, we determine the most favorable adsorption site for Mn and identify a stable half-metallic ferromagnetic ground state within the optimized configuration.

Sgr A East is a stellar explosion remnant situated near the Galactic Center, whose origin remains uncertain. This study examines the feasibility of generating the remnant from the collapse of a single star by analyzing the required mass ejection and the resulting stellar dynamics. Our findings indicate that creating Sgr A East from a solitary stellar collapse demands an ejection of approximately $10^3$ solar masses. This massive loss of material would result in the ejection of the star's gravitational binding energy, a scenario incompatible with formation via a single star. These results imply that Sgr A East is instead a merger remnant, a conclusion that aligns with the presence of a compact radio source at the remnant's center.

In the text-categorization domain, the prevalence of over-represented majority classes often overshadows significantly under-represented minority ones. Consequently, this study evaluates the impact of various oversampling strategies applied to minority classes within a multi-class setting. To assess these methods, we developed an original benchmark suite comprising 11 datasets and 12 diverse machine learning algorithms. Our findings demonstrate that the performance benefits provided by oversampling are consistent and robust across nearly all datasets and almost every algorithm tested.

In the U.S., COVID-19 has claimed over 600,000 lives, while media coverage has played a pivotal role in shaping public perception. This study examines the interaction between news coverage and audience engagement regarding the pandemic in 2020. Utilizing an open-access news feed, researchers analyzed the evolution of regional coverage, case counts, mortality rates, and public interest across all 50 states throughout 2020. The findings reveal that while COVID coverage and engagement correlate with both infections and deaths, the relationship is notably stronger with case counts. Furthermore, an inverse correlation exists between news coverage and regional engagement, suggesting that areas with higher reporting receive less audience attention.

The Rapid Multipole Method (RMM) serves as a highly efficient algorithm for accelerating Coulomb interactions within periodic systems, including crystals. A distinctive feature of this technique is its ability to preserve the total angular momentum of the system, a conservation law that can be utilized to further accelerate electronic structure calculations. This study presents an updated version of the RMM that maintains exact angular momentum preservation to a higher level, making it compatible with any choice of basis functions. Additionally, the research introduces a novel implementation of the method within the code package.

This study examines the shift in polarization from the initial to the final proton within elastic electron-proton scattering, $e\vec{p} \to e\vec{p}$. We demonstrate that this polarization transfer is intrinsically linked to the ratio of longitudinal to transverse virtual photon fluxes. Furthermore, our analysis indicates that this effect is amplified at lower momentum transfers ($Q^2$) and energy transfers ($Q^2/\nu^2$).

In scenarios where data access is restricted, a common strategy involves leveraging data-generated authorities to create synthetic samples for boosting training data. However, existing approaches suffer from critical flaws: they either fail to ensure the synthetic records share the same distribution as the original training data, or they depend on non-parametric models that are difficult to integrate into standard data pipelines. To address these issues, this paper introduces a new paradigm utilizing parametric data-generation authors capable of boosting effective information flow for specific tasks. We further present Cost-Effective Data-Amplification (CEDA), a method designed to produce synthetic samples that align distributionally with training datasets while maintaining computational efficiency. Extensive experiments on various classification and clustering tasks demonstrate that CEA consistently outperforms competing methods, delivering significant improvements in accuracy and robustness.

This study reports an analysis of the Higgs boson pair ($\text{HH}$) production via vector boson fusion (VBF), focusing on a decay mode where one Higgs boson radiates a W boson ($\text{W}\text{H}\text{H}$). The investigation utilizes an integrated luminosity of $139\,\text{fb}^{-1}$ from proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of $13\,\text{TeV}$, gathered by the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider. The search targets the $\text{W}\to\ell\nu$ and $\text{H}\to\text{bb}$ decay channels, employing an analysis strategy that divides the sample into two exclusive signal regions: one requiring two same-sign leptons and another with exactly one lepton-pair pair. These regions are defined by the presence of at least two forward jets exhibiting high dijet mass, alongside one or two additional b-tagged jets. The event selection relies on a multivariate technique to isolate signal events from background noise. The findings are interpreted within the context of the Standard Model, yielding an upper limit on the VBF+SS (double Higgs) cross-section that is approximately $2.5$ times the SM expectation, with an upper limit of $2.5$ pb at the 95% confidence level.

Light-based technologies are fundamental to modern society, yet the development of new laser types has largely stalled since the introduction of alkali-based spin lasers nearly a hundred years ago. We propose a concept for an all-electric alkali spin laser that utilizes spin-exchange collisions to generate self-rotating spin fields. These fields, in turn, cause rapid circular polarization switching in an optical transition occurring within an external electronic environment. This system operates by driving the laser medium with purely electronic energy, thereby eliminating the need for a cooling laser and potentially enabling significantly faster modulation speeds. Such advancements could substantially expand the functional capabilities and operational flexibility of devices utilizing the photonic effects.

We investigate the local connectivity of the locus of polarized K3 surfaces, denoted as $S_\lambda = (\pi^{-1}(\lambda), \phi)$, where $\pi: S \to S$ is Kummer surface family and $\phi$ is the ample class of $H^2(S,S)$. This research explores the Picard locus's behavior near cuspidal points within the Kummer surface family surface context. Specifically, we prove that the Picard locus exhibits a Siegel disk component near a cusp, signifying the presence of a Kummer surface family surface with Picard value 10 and specific Picard value 10 and structure. These findings have significant implications for understanding the Picard value and structure of Kummer surface families.

We propose a model in which dark matter is composed of the lighter neutralino, which decomposes into a sterile neutrino and a long-lived neutral scalar. These long-lived scalars subsequently decay into a pair of dark pions, which subsequently decay into Standard Model pions and photons. The model is consistent with current experimental constraints and predicts a lighter scalar with a mass below 1 GeV. The predicted gamma radiation spectrum from the decay chain is distinct from the signals produced by non-decaying neutralino dark matter models.

Estimating the genus of a simple graph is NP-hard, and the existing polynomial algorithms suffer from a bit-size complexity that escalates rapidly with the input parameter. In 2017, Kr\'{a}l, Norin, and Pikhurko established that estimating genus is NP-hard even within multiplicative factors of $o(\log g)$. In contrast, this study presents an effective, polynomial-time algorithm capable of estimating the genus of dense graphs to within an $o(\log g)$ multiplicative error.

We introduce and analyze a randomized Newton method designed for distributed convex optimization over a fixed network. Our approach addresses the dual of the original problem, leveraging dual variables to eliminate explicit dependencies on the network topology, and then applies a stochastic selection of coordinates within this domain to reduce communication. Compared to conventional dual coordinate descent methods, the randomization enables further compression of the communication payload. We establish the convergence rate of the proposed algorithm for instances where the objective is self-concordant and demonstrate that it achieves optimal performance in the aggregate of curvature assumptions and computational complexity.

This study presents a novel dataset comprising Bengali and Hindi comments extracted from various social media platforms, along with baseline models trained to classify them as hate speech or not. We provide a detailed breakdown of the dataset's composition, including an analysis of the most prevalent bigrams within the Bengali and Hindi hate speech subcategories. Furthermore, we train several baseline models to identify hate speech in both languages, evaluating their performance using traditional metrics. We also assess the effectiveness of transfer learning by applying models trained on the English Hate Speech Dataset to these languages. Finally, we analyze the outcomes of our experiments and draw conclusions based on the results.

A primary hurdle in assessing machine learning models lies in the difficulty of defining and measuring success, a challenge that is especially acute when training data lacks a consistent quality metric. This issue is particularly acute in driving record prediction models used for setting insurance premiums and determining commercial vehicle insurance eligibility, where historical data often fails to reflect fairness. Because historical underwriting practices have historically been biased, such records cannot reliably evaluate current fairness in automated decision-making. Consequently, we propose utilizing contextualized expert knowledge to establish reliable evaluation metrics for these models. By incorporating situational details into the assessment process, we can develop a metric grounded in professional judgment rather than historical inequity. To validate this approach, we conducted interviews with underwriters and analyzed their decision-making logic to create an assessment grounded in their expertise. Our key finding indicates that while overall claim history is a significant factor, its impact is heavily modulated by the specific context of claims, particularly those related to parking locations.

The Sinkhorn algorithm serves as a practical iteration for addressing the Schr\"odinger problem, which aims to determine two probability measures, $\mu$ and $\nu$, such that the product $\nu \otimes \mu$ is consistent with a given cost function $c$ through the relation $e^{-c} = \gamma * p$, where $*$ denotes element-wise multiplication and $p$ is a fixed matrix. The cross-section for the creation of top quark pairs ($t\bar{t}$) in proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s} = 5.02$ TeV has been determined using data collected by the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider, accumulating an integrated luminosity of $25.3$ fb$^{-1}$. Human social and economic activity are closely linked to macroeconomic trends, and understanding pandemic dynamics requires examining shifts in urban activity alongside economic data. This study analyzes spatiotemporal patterns of urban engagement in New York City throughout the pandemic using mobile phone records, finding that the economic downturn intensified the divide in resident interactions across different income brackets. While wealthier residents maintained consistent activity levels, those with lower incomes experienced a sharper decline in mobility. Furthermore, the pandemic accelerated the adoption of remote work, which further widened the gap between high- and low-income residents in their physical activity patterns.

This study evaluates the field-split preconditioner within a dual-phase flow solver, specifically analyzing the impact of split nonlinearities on the speed of dual-phase flow solver convergence. Results indicate that one of the field-split methods consistently outperforms the other across all scenarios, including those involving heterogeneous porous media matrices. Unilateral devices, which permit optical signals to travel in only one direction, are inherently based on non-reciprocal components. In this study, we present a configuration utilizing reciprocal elements that sustains unidirectional propagation by integrating a resonance cavity with an aperture. Our findings indicate that as the aperture dimensions decrease, the system exhibits enhanced asymmetry in transmission, along with a significant boost in the amplification of certain modes. Furthermore, the device demonstrates the potential to act as an optical isolator, with the ability to function as a chiral cavity that supports standing waves formed exclusively by chiral modes.

This work examines the relationship between two-surface Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) gravity and the non-compact CFT known as Liouville theory. Tip-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (TERS) merges the high spectral resolution of Raman spectroscopy with the spatial precision offered by scanning probe microscopy. This technique achieves sub-molecular imaging by leveraging a scanning metallic tip to amplify the local electromagnetic field. While numerous experimental and theoretical studies have explored TERS, a comprehensive understanding of the interplay between electronic transitions and electromagnetic enhancement remains elusive. Reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms have been used to model the neural coding of reward learning and predictability. However, these algorithms typically do not account for strategies that emerge when agents select among multiple equivalent options. We propose a new model that integrates the characteristics of multi-armed bandit tasks with existing algorithms, incorporating exploration, suboptimality, and inaction. Our findings, supported by human behavioral data and monkey neurophysiological recordings, reveal a strong correlation between the prevalence of such non-standard strategies and the neural representation of reward prediction errors in the midbrain.

To support these findings, we provide $E_8$-lattice vectors that satisfy the anticommutation relations required for the complexified $E_8$ Pauli matrices.

Estimating close neighbor distance is crucial for indexing time series, particularly when the Euclidean distance proves inadequate. This paper introduces two novel algorithms that efficiently compute the Fréchet distance between points within a polylogarithmic time complexity relative to the series length. Additionally, we present an experimental analysis comparing these algorithms against standard distance metrics—including Edit, Editel, Editel distance measures such as the Edit distance, and variants like the Edit distance, and various other edit-based metrics.
